replication.target_description: Study 1, five-to-eight-month-old infants; right posterior temporal channel 18 peak HbO change 10–25 s after stimulus onset, paired social dynamic versus nonsocial dynamic conditions. Same paradigm as original Experiment 2, with broader infant age range.

n.sample_role: Infants with usable channel 18 data; paired test df = 17 and channel-specific N = 18 printed in the adjacent temperament analysis.
n.exclusions: 32 additional infants excluded: 17 for insufficient looking, 15 for no usable relevant channels. Further channel-specific rejection for CV >10%, gain >8, or absent heartbeat; at least three valid trials per condition required. Overall retained 37 is not the target channel analytic n.

notes: Original title verified against publisher PDF; cache contains relevant pages from the primary publisher PDF parse. Original source is available. Original page 9 covers multiple tests: right posterior channel 28 selected to align with the replication right posterior contrast, but hemisphere is not uniquely specified by the input, so original target_match remains unknown. The same original paired comparison at left channel 14 prints t = −2.15, p = .04 and mean nonsocial-minus-social change −0.88 μM; right channel 28 prints mean change −1.15 μM. These are separate channel tests, not pooled effects. Original effect direction is nonsocial-minus-social, replication social-minus-nonsocial. Replication Table 1 labels p-values FDR-corrected and prints 0.048 for t = 3.15, df = 17; section 3.2 prose prints p = 0.006 for that same test. Table value retained with discrepancy explicit. Replication primary full text has a correction notice; no separate correction document inspected. Authors describe replication success while explaining that only the right hemisphere was significant, unlike the original bilateral result. No effect metric conversions performed.
